quote_json: "zero (in which latter case the sign and scale will be 0)"
notes: A decimal real literal keeps its apparent scale 'unless the value is rounded or the value is zero (in which latter case the sign and scale will be 0)' (PDF p. 73 lines 9-14), so 0.000000m is the decimal with sign 0, coefficient 0 and scale 0. The zero exception is explicit 1st-edition text and the 7th edition's 6.4.5.4 drops it ('preserved unless the value is rounded', PDF p. 54); the observer Decimal.GetBits belongs to the library the 1st edition incorporates by reference (PDF p. 389 lines 2-6; listed at PDF p. 407 line 15), with its bit representation checked by the nonzero decimal control. The 0.731000m mutant keeps scale 6 under the 1st edition and fails, isolating the zero value. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

9.3.1's new-line is only U+000D, U+000A, U+000D U+000A, U+2028 and U+2029 (PDF p. 66 lines 32-37) and whitespace is only class Zs, HT, VT and FF (PDF p. 68 lines 5-11), while every source file must conform to the input grammar of whitespace, comments, tokens and new-lines (PDF p. 66 lines 2-18), so a raw U+0085 between tokens violates the lexical grammar and clause 2 requires a diagnostic (PDF p. 17 lines 33-35). UTF-8 input must decode to U+0085 (PDF p. 65 lines 11-12), and U+0085 (class Cc) is not whitespace, not an identifier-part-character (PDF p. 69 lines 28-48), not a token and not a new-line, so the line matches no input-section-part; the 7th edition adds it to New_Line (6.3.2-6.3.3), a later change. The NEL-to-space repair is exactly the valid witness, so the rejection is attributable to the NEL alone. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

single-line-comment is '// input-charactersopt', input-character is 'Any Unicode character except a new-line-character', and new-line-character is only U+000D, U+000A, U+2028 and U+2029 (PDF p. 67 lines 28-39), so the comment runs through U+0085 to the end of the physical line. Under the 1st edition the assignment after the NEL is comment text, value stays 43 and the program prints OK 1; the 7th edition's Input_Character excludes U+0085 (6.3.3), which is what csc implements. The NEL-to-LF mutant must print FAIL under the 1st edition, so the check isolates the NEL. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

single-character is 'Any character except ' (U+0027), \ (U+005C), and new-line-character' (PDF p. 73 lines 27-28), and new-line-character is only U+000D, U+000A, U+2028 and U+2029 (PDF p. 67 lines 35-39), so a raw U+0085 between quotes is a char literal of value 133. The 1st edition's exclusion names new-line-character, which lacks NEL, and the UTF-8 source must decode to U+0085 (PDF p. 65 lines 11-12); the 7th edition's Single_Character excludes U+0085 explicitly (6.4.5.5), a later change. The NEL-to-Z mutant must fail the value check. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

single-regular-string-literal-character is 'Any character except " (U+0022), \ (U+005C), and new-line-character' (PDF p. 74 lines 26-27), whose new-line-character set lacks U+0085 (PDF p. 67 lines 35-39), so "a<U+0085>b" is a three-character string with U+0085 at index 1. The 1st edition's exclusion names only new-line-character, while the 7th edition's Single_Regular_String_Literal_Character excludes U+0085 (6.4.5.6), a later change. The NEL-to-Z mutant must fail the value check, isolating the NEL. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

pp-declaration is 'whitespaceopt # whitespaceopt define whitespace conditional-symbol pp-new-line' and pp-new-line is 'whitespaceopt single-line-commentopt new-line' (PDF p. 78 lines 13-17), with new-line lacking U+0085 (PDF p. 66 lines 32-37), so '#define Active<U+0085>class Entry ...' is a malformed directive that clause 2 requires to be diagnosed (PDF p. 17 lines 33-35). U+0085 is neither whitespace (PDF p. 68 lines 5-11) nor part of a conditional-symbol, which is an identifier-or-keyword (PDF p. 77 lines 17-18; PDF p. 69 lines 28-48), so nothing after 'Active' can match pp-new-line; the 7th edition's PP_New_Line uses the widened New_Line (6.5.1). The NEL-to-LF repair is the valid witness, isolating the NEL. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

pp-message is 'whitespace input-charactersopt new-line' (PDF p. 81 lines 33-38) and input-character excludes only U+000D, U+000A, U+2028 and U+2029 (PDF p. 67 lines 33-39), so the #warning message runs through U+0085 and '#define Enabled' to the end of the physical line and Enabled is never defined. Under the 1st edition the program prints OK 1, while the 7th edition's Input_Character excludes U+0085 (6.5.6). The payload check also assumes the warning reports its pp-message, which the normative 'generate error and warning messages' (PDF p. 81 lines 31-32) implies and the informative example (lines 45-48) shows, but the runtime check carries the requirement alone; the NEL-to-LF mutant fails both checks. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

file-name-character is 'Any character except " (U+0022), and new-line' (PDF p. 82 lines 28-34), new-line lacks U+0085 (PDF p. 66 lines 32-37), and the compiler must treat the next line as having the given line number and file name (PDF p. 82 lines 35-37), so the #warning after '#line 61 "map<U+0085>unit.cs"' is reported at that file name, line 61. The reading is right, csc departs (the 7th edition's PP_Compilation_Unit_Name_Character excludes U+0085, 6.5.8), and the original program is a sound test. But the mutation 'unit.cs' to 'other.cs' leaves the raw NEL in place: original and mutant differ only in ASCII file-name text, and csc refuses both for the same NEL, so the mutation exercises the file-name oracle rather than the construct. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

line-indicator is 'decimal-digits whitespace file-name' with no stated maximum (PDF p. 82 lines 24-27), and for a non-default indicator 'the compiler treats the line after the directive as having the given line number (and file name, if specified)' (PDF p. 82 lines 35-37). Nothing in the 1st edition caps decimal-digits: Annex B's implementation-defined list has no line limit (PDF p. 380 lines 1-15), and clause 1's capacity remark is informative and about program size (PDF p. 15 lines 14-15), whereas the 7th edition makes the maximum implementation-defined (6.5.8, PDF p. 67). The extra CS1687 warning is permitted; the dropped mapping is the departure, and the 20000001 mutant must fail the exact-line check. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

An unsuffixed literal takes the first of int, uint, long, ulong that holds its value (PDF p. 72 lines 13-15), the int -2147483648 exception covers only a decimal-integer-literal (PDF p. 72 lines 25-29), and negating a uint operand converts it to long with a long result, the exception again being only the decimal literal (PDF p. 169 lines 3-5). 0x80000000 is uint, so -0x80000000 is a long constant; no implicit constant conversion takes long to int (PDF p. 129 lines 6-11), so only Pick(long) applies and returns 2. The 7th edition's 6.4.5.3 widens the exception to any Integer_Literal (PDF p. 53) while its 12.9.3 still says decimal (PDF p. 257); that later change does not reach ISO-1, and the decimal mutant must select Pick(int) and fail. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

0x8000000000000000 fits only ulong (PDF p. 72 lines 13-15), the long -9223372036854775808 exception covers only a decimal-integer-literal (PDF p. 72 lines 30-33), and 'If the operand of the negation operator is of type ulong, a compile-time error occurs', excepting only that decimal literal (PDF p. 169 lines 6-8). Both the lexical and the unary-minus clause of the 1st edition make this negation a compile-time error; the 7th edition's 6.4.5.3 extends the exception to any Integer_Literal (PDF p. 53), a later change. The decimal mutant is the valid witness, so the rejection is attributable to the hexadecimal spelling alone. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

ed1-9.4.2-005: At ISO-1, int \u005fslot = 8; is a compile-time error, because no identifier-start-character matches an escape for U+005F; the literal repair _slot compiles and prints 8. Use the short \u005f spelling as the witness: the 7th-edition grammar also omits \U0000005F, so the long spelling (also an error at ISO-1) does not isolate the 1st/7th difference. The exact original and positive witness were observed once at levels 1 and 7.3; the latter level is comparative evidence, not an assertion of first-edition authority there. Failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.
